task: Create a truthful, read-only architecture explainer for the Agentic Life OS publication candidate.
audience: Developers, researchers, practitioners, and future private-instance operators
first_read: A local-first life OS is useful because it knows where public code stops and private authority begins.

references.label: Agentic Life OS public/private boundary
references.reason: Canonical release state and system boundary.

references.label: Manrope and IBM Plex Mono
references.reason: Selected for calm operational intelligence; local-only sources preserve the no-subresource boundary.

references.label: Independent accessibility audit
references.reason: Drove truthfulness, semantics, focus, contrast, and deployment-header corrections.

direction.signature: Five governed layers presented as an inspectable safety boundary, not a command center.
system: Dark mineral surface with restrained amber and teal signals
No scripts, forms, analytics, client storage, or application subresources
Responsive single-column collapse and reduced-motion-safe static behavior

asset_quality.why_premium: An exact semantic interface is the correct primary asset for a technical architecture explainer.

artifacts.notes: Source and accessibility semantics reviewed; actual desktop/mobile browser export inspection remains blocked by the current machine/storage gate.

checks.name: asset-tier
checks.evidence: Tier C exact interface selected; decorative media is not needed for the architecture surface.

checks.name: accessibility-source-review
checks.evidence: Independent review corrections include semantic ol/li ordering, skip-target focus, high-contrast focus-visible, stronger boundaries, larger labels, and truthful role wording.

checks.name: export-inspection
checks.evidence: No desktop/mobile browser capture was produced under the current resource gate.

checks.name: visual-qa
checks.evidence: Visual, forced-colors, zoom, and screen-reader runtime inspection remain release gates.

score.notes: Strong truthfulness, hierarchy, semantics, and boundary design; runtime visual inspection and host-header verification are still outstanding.

known_risks: The dashboard is not approved for public hosting.
Anti-framing and other defense-in-depth headers must be configured and inspected at the host.
Actual desktop, mobile, keyboard, forced-colors, zoom, and screen-reader QA remain incomplete.
